signature: SUBROUTINE DLATRS3( UPLO, TRANS, DIAG, NORMIN, N, NRHS, A, LDA,

params.name: uplo
params.reference:
Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower triangular.

-   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
-   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular

params.name: trans
params.reference:
Specifies the operation applied to A.

-   `= 'N'`: Solve $A \, x = s \, b$  (No transpose)
-   `= 'T'`: Solve $A^T \, x = s \, b$  (Transpose)
-   `= 'C'`: Solve $A^T \, x = s \, b$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)

params.name: diag
params.reference:
Specifies whether or not the matrix A is unit triangular.

-   `= 'N'`: Non-unit triangular
-   `= 'U'`: Unit triangular

params.name: normin
params.reference:
Specifies whether `CNORM` has been set or not.

-   `= 'Y'`: `CNORM` contains the column norms on entry
-   `= 'N'`: `CNORM` is not set on entry.  On exit, the norms will be computed and stored in `CNORM`.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: nrhs
params.reference: The number of columns of X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: The triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading n by n upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading n by n lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. If `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are also not referenced and are assumed to be 1.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max$ (1,N).

params.name: X
params.reference: On entry, the right hand side B of the triangular system. On exit, X is overwritten by the solution matrix X.

params.name: ldx
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array X. $\mathrm{LDX} \ge \max$ (1,N).

params.name: SCALE
params.reference: The scaling factor s(k) is for the triangular system $A \, x(:,k) = s(k) \, b(:,k)$ or $A^T \, x(:,k) = s(k) \, b(:,k)$. If `SCALE = 0`, the matrix A is singular or badly scaled. If $A(j,j) = 0$ is encountered, a non-trivial vector x(:,k) that is an exact or approximate solution to $A \, x(:,k) = 0$ is returned. If the system so badly scaled that solution cannot be presented as $x(:,k) \cdot 1/s(k)$, then $x(:,k) = 0$ is returned.

params.name: CNORM
params.reference:
If `NORMIN = 'Y'`, `CNORM` is an input argument and `CNORM(j)` contains the norm of the off-diagonal part of the j-th column of A. If `TRANS = 'N'`, `CNORM(j)` must be greater than or equal to the infinity-norm, and if `TRANS = 'T'` or 'C', `CNORM(j)` must be greater than or equal to the 1-norm.

If `NORMIN = 'N'`, `CNORM` is an output argument and `CNORM(j)` returns the 1-norm of the offdiagonal part of the j-th column of A.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal size of `WORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
`LWORK` \>= MAX(1, $2 \, \mathrm{NBA} \, \max (\mathrm{NBA}, \min (\mathrm{NRHS}, 32))$, where $\mathrm{NBA} = (N + \mathrm{NB} - 1)/\mathrm{NB}$ and NB is the optimal block size.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal dimensions of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -k`, the k-th argument had an illegal value

notes: argument INFO is not in the doc comment; type from its declaration
workspace check for LWORK not reducible to a minimum: .NOT.LQUERY .AND. LWORK.LT.WORK( 1 )
